title: Data Interception in Transit
description: Assignment data (including student ID, course, timestamp) could be intercepted during transmission if not properly encrypted.
assumptions: Assumes TLS/HTTPS is not enforced or has vulnerabilities.

title: Insecure Data Storage
description: Submitted assignment data may be stored insecurely, risking unauthorized access.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient access controls or encryption at rest.

title: Identification via Data in Transit
description: Student ID transmitted in plaintext could allow identification if intercepted.
assumptions: Assumes lack of encryption or tokenization during transmission.

title: Identification via Stored Data
description: Stored student ID and submission details could enable identification if accessed unauthorizedly.
assumptions: Assumes inadequate access controls on stored data.

title: Linkability of Submission Data
description: Submission data could be linked with other student records to build profiles.
assumptions: Assumes data is combined across courses or systems without consent.

title: Data Misuse for Secondary Purposes
description: Submission data may be used beyond educational purposes (e.g., analytics, third-party sharing).
assumptions: Assumes lack of clear data usage policies or consent mechanisms.

title: Lack of Awareness of Data Usage
description: Students may not understand how their submission data is processed or shared.
assumptions: Assumes privacy notices are unclear or not prominently displayed.

title: Non-Compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: Data handling may violate regulations (e.g., GDPR, FERPA) if not properly managed.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient compliance measures or audits.

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Submissions
description: Students could deny submitting assignments if proper audit logs are not maintained.
assumptions: Assumes inadequate logging or authentication of submissions.

title: Student identifier transmitted in data flow
description: The data flow contains student ID, which is a unique reference to the identity of the data subject. This enables direct identification of students from the data in transit.
assumptions: Student ID is a persistent unique identifier for each student

title: Linkability of student activities across systems
description: The student ID in this flow can be used to link this submission/grading request to other data about the same student in the Assignment & Grading Service or other systems, enabling correlation of student activities.
assumptions: Student ID is used consistently across multiple systems

title: Non-repudiation of student submission
description: The Assignment & Grading Service receives and processes identified data including student ID and file reference, creating evidence that could prevent a student from denying their involvement in a submission or grading request.
assumptions: P2 stores or logs the received data as evidence of submission
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether P2 retains this data as audit evidence

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student data in transit
description: Student ID, course information, and file references transmitted between P1 and P2 could be intercepted by unauthorized parties if the flow is not properly secured.
assumptions: Data flow may be vulnerable to interception without encryption
uncertainty_note: Severity depends on transport security measures in place

title: Student Identifiability in Assignment Storage
description: The grading service includes student ID in the data sent to the assignment store, making students directly identifiable from stored data. This creates identifiability risks if the data store is accessed by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Student ID is a direct personal identifier

title: Potential Non-Minimal Data Collection
description: The grading service stores assignment files with student ID, course, and submission time. This may exceed the minimal data necessary for grading purposes, constituting implicit data disclosure if all fields are not strictly required.
assumptions: Not all stored fields are strictly necessary for the grading function
uncertainty_note: Uncertain whether all data fields are minimally required for the stated purpose

title: Linkability of Student Data Across Systems
description: Student IDs stored in the assignment store can be used to link this data with other student records in the system, potentially creating comprehensive student profiles beyond the original purpose of assignment storage.
assumptions: Student IDs are used consistently across multiple system components

title: Teacher identity disclosed during login
description: The teacher's identifying credentials (username, password, or authentication tokens) are transmitted during login, making their identity available to the system.
assumptions: Standard authentication mechanism is used

title: Teacher activity linkable through request metadata
description: The data flow contains metadata (source IP, timestamp, session ID) that could be used to link the teacher's identity to their review activity and timing.
assumptions: Network traffic is observable by third parties

title: Authentication credentials intercepted in transit
description: Login credentials or session tokens transmitted over the data flow could be intercepted by network attackers if not properly encrypted.
assumptions: Transport layer security may be misconfigured or absent

title: Processing of identified teacher data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes and stores the teacher's identifying information along with their review activity, creating a record linking the teacher to specific submissions.
assumptions: System logs teacher activity with identifying information

title: Unauthorized access to teacher review data
description: The process could expose teacher identity and review activity to unauthorized users through inadequate access controls or data breaches.
assumptions: Access control mechanisms may have vulnerabilities

title: Linkability of student identities to submissions
description: Teacher receives student names paired with work content and submission times, enabling linking of individual student identities to their academic submissions and performance data.
assumptions: Teacher has access to the portal and can view all student submissions

title: Identifiability of students
description: Student names are directly transmitted to the teacher, making individual students identifiable from the data received.
assumptions: Student names are included in the submission data

title: Unauthorized disclosure in transit
description: Student submission data (names, work content, times) could be intercepted during transmission between portal and teacher if not properly encrypted.
assumptions: Data flow may lack end-to-end encryption or secure transport

title: Student unawareness of data sharing
description: Students may not be aware that their submission data including names and work content is being shared with teachers through the portal.
assumptions: Consent or notification mechanisms may be insufficient

title: Potential non-compliance with educational privacy regulations
description: Portal's sharing of student data with teachers may not fully comply with educational privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) regarding data minimization and purpose limitation.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements apply to educational data processing
uncertainty_note: Specific regulatory framework depends on jurisdiction

title: Student Identifiability at Source
description: Teacher submits student IDs along with grades and feedback, directly identifying individual students in the data being shared.
assumptions: Student IDs are unique identifiers that can be used to identify specific students.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure in Transit
description: Grade data, feedback text, and student IDs transmitted over the network could be intercepted by unauthorized parties if not properly encrypted.
assumptions: Data flows over network infrastructure that could be vulnerable to interception.

title: Data Integrity Compromise in Transit
description: Grades and feedback could be modified during transmission without detection, leading to inaccurate academic records.
assumptions: Network transmission lacks integrity verification mechanisms.

title: Linkability of Student Records
description: Grades Portal receives and stores student IDs with grades/feedback, enabling linking of student performance data across multiple assignments and contexts.
assumptions: Portal stores data persistently and can correlate records by student ID.

title: Unauthorized Access at Destination
description: Grades Portal may not properly restrict access to stored grade data, allowing unauthorized users to view student grades and feedback.
assumptions: Portal has access control mechanisms that could be misconfigured or bypassed.

title: Non-repudiation of Grading Actions
description: Portal may not maintain adequate audit logs of which teacher submitted which grades, allowing teachers to deny their grading actions.
assumptions: System logging may be insufficient or not tamper-proof.

title: Processing of identified student data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes identified student data (student identity linked to grades and feedback). While this is necessary for the system function, it creates a privacy risk if the identified data is not properly protected or if access controls fail.
assumptions: Student authentication is required to access grades; the system maintains a link between student identity and their academic records.

title: Unauthorized interception of grades data in transit
description: Student grades and feedback transmitted over the network could be intercepted by unauthorized parties if the communication channel is not properly secured (e.g., missing TLS/encryption).
assumptions: Data flows over network infrastructure that could be monitored or intercepted.

title: Unauthorized access to student grades at destination
description: The Grades Portal Web App could expose student grades to unauthorized users through inadequate access controls, privilege escalation, or data leakage vulnerabilities.
assumptions: The process stores or displays grades that could be accessed by unauthorized parties if security controls fail.

title: Student unaware of data processing scope
description: The student may not be fully aware of what data is being collected, how long it is retained, or what secondary processing occurs when requesting their grades.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all data processing activities associated with grade retrieval.

title: Interception of grades in transit
description: Student grades and teacher feedback transmitted over the network could be intercepted by unauthorized parties if the connection is not properly encrypted (e.g., missing HTTPS/TLS).
assumptions: Assumes network transmission occurs over potentially insecure channels

title: Student identification through flow metadata
description: Network monitoring of the data flow could reveal which student is accessing the grades portal, potentially linking the student to their academic performance even without seeing the actual grades.
assumptions: Assumes network traffic can be monitored by third parties

title: Linkability through access logging
description: The portal's logging of which student accessed which grades could create linkability between the student's identity and their academic performance, potentially correlating with other logged activities.
assumptions: Assumes the portal maintains access logs

title: Incorrect grades displayed to student
description: The portal could display incorrect or tampered grades to the student due to bugs, unauthorized modifications, or data corruption in the source system.
assumptions: Assumes potential for data integrity issues in the portal or backend systems

title: Student could deny receiving grades
description: Without proper receipt confirmation mechanisms, a student could deny having received their grades or feedback, creating non-repudiation issues for academic records.
assumptions: Assumes no formal receipt acknowledgment system exists

title: Unencrypted Credentials in Transit
description: Parent's login credentials and request data may be transmitted without encryption, allowing interception and identification of the parent.
assumptions: Assumes no TLS/HTTPS is enforced for this flow.
uncertainty_note: Context does not specify encryption status; threat applies if credentials are sent in plaintext.

title: Unauthorized Access to Child's Grades
description: Grades Portal Web App may fail to validate parent's authorization, allowing access to grades beyond the linked child account.
assumptions: Assumes access control mechanisms are not properly implemented or enforced.
uncertainty_note: Context does not specify access control details; threat applies if authorization checks are bypassed.

title: Unauthorized disclosure due to weak authentication
description: Portal may not properly verify parent's identity before sharing child's data, leading to unauthorized access.

title: Data interception in transit
description: Grades data transmitted without encryption could be intercepted by attackers.

title: Linkability via metadata
description: Communication metadata may allow linking parent to child, compromising anonymity.

title: Data misuse by parent
description: Parent may use child's data for unintended purposes, such as sharing with third parties.

title: Linkability of parent-child relationships
description: Administrator creates and modifies parent-child links with names, emails, and relationships, enabling linking of individuals across the system.
assumptions: Administrator has access to relationship data that can be used to link family members

title: Direct identifiability through personal data
description: Administrator provides names and emails when creating/modifying accounts, which are directly identifying information.
assumptions: Names and emails are provided as part of account creation

title: Unauthorized disclosure of account data in transit
description: Account information (names, emails, roles, relationships) transmitted from administrator to web app could be intercepted.
assumptions: Data transmission occurs over network without guaranteed encryption

title: Data integrity compromise during transmission
description: Account and relationship data could be modified in transit between administrator and web app.
assumptions: Data transmission lacks integrity protection mechanisms

title: Linkability through stored relationship data
description: Grades Portal stores parent-child links enabling linking of individuals across the system for profiling or tracking.
assumptions: Web app stores relationship data in a queryable format

title: Unauthorized disclosure from web app storage
description: Account data (names, emails, roles, relationships) stored in the web app could be accessed by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Web app has potential access control vulnerabilities

title: Unauthorized modification of account data
description: Account and relationship data stored in the web app could be modified without proper authorization.
assumptions: Web app may have insufficient access controls on data modification

title: Unawareness of data processing by parents/children
description: Parents and children may not be aware that their relationship data and personal information is being processed and stored.
assumptions: Consent and transparency mechanisms may be insufficient

title: Parent-child relationship data enables family member linking
description: Account directory stores parent-child relationship links, enabling correlation of academic records across family members and creating linkability between students and their parents
assumptions: Account directory retains relationship data that can be queried to link family members

title: Account records contain identifiable student/parent information
description: Account directory stores account records with personally identifiable information about students and parents that could be used to identify individuals
assumptions: Account records contain PII such as names, IDs, or other identifying information

title: Unauthorized access to account directory exposes sensitive student data
description: Account directory containing student and parent information could be accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to disclosure of sensitive educational data
assumptions: Account directory has access controls that could be bypassed or misconfigured

title: Users unaware of parent-child relationship data storage
description: Students and parents may not be informed that their relationship links are being written to and stored in the account directory
assumptions: Privacy notices or consent mechanisms do not explicitly cover relationship data storage

title: Account directory may violate educational data protection regulations
description: Storage of student and parent relationship data may not comply with FERPA, GDPR, or other applicable educational data protection regulations
assumptions: Account directory storage practices may not meet regulatory requirements for educational data
uncertainty_note: Regulatory compliance depends on specific jurisdiction and implementation details

title: Data in transit could be intercepted
description: Account records and relationship links transmitted from grading service to account directory could be intercepted during transmission
assumptions: Data flow may not use encryption or secure transmission protocols

title: Data in transit could be modified
description: Account records and relationship links could be altered during transmission from grading service to account directory
assumptions: Data flow may lack integrity protection mechanisms

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades
description: The Assignment & Grading Service may expose grade records to unauthorized parties when building student, parent, and teacher views. Grade data is sensitive PII that requires strict access controls.
assumptions: Service has proper authentication and authorization mechanisms

title: Student identifiability in grade views
description: Grade records are inherently identifiable to specific students. When the service builds views for different stakeholders, student identities may be exposed beyond intended recipients.
assumptions: Views are properly scoped to authorized users only

title: Data aggregation privacy risks
description: The service aggregates grade records to build comprehensive views for students, parents, and teachers. This aggregation could reveal patterns or information not intended to be disclosed.
assumptions: Aggregation logic respects privacy boundaries

title: FERPA compliance risks in grade data processing
description: Grade records are subject to FERPA and educational privacy regulations. The service's processing of grade data for multiple view types may not fully comply with regulatory requirements.
assumptions: Service implements FERPA-compliant access controls
uncertainty_note: Regulatory compliance depends on specific implementation details not fully specified

title: Grade data interception in transit
description: Grade records transmitted from the database to the grading service could be intercepted if the data flow is not properly encrypted.
assumptions: Data flow uses encryption in transit
